text:
maria: :rotating_light: Seeing a spike in CUDA OOMs on cluster-gpu-22, reports came in ~now. Error pattern: CUDA OOM during model serve step despite reported headroom. Root logs show repeated allocator failures with reserved blocks intact.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421. Severity: P1. Pager notified @dylan (oncall).
maria: Key symptoms — containers not restarting, requests returning 503, some requests hit fallback model. Affected: 3 tenants (acct-110, acct-221, acct-305) with elevated error rates and latencies.
dylan: I'm on it. Can someone paste the nvidia-smi and allocator state?
kai: Pasting quick snapshot from node-gpu-22:```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 530.41.01    Driver Version: 530.41.01    CUDA Version: 12.0     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A40           On         | 00000000:65:00.0 Off | N/A                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
|  PID   Type   Process name                             Usage      |
| 12345  C      python serve.py                            35634MiB   |
| 22345  C      python aux_worker                           2048MiB   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

kai: Allocator dump shows large number of small free chunks, heavy fragmentation. Reserved pool size: 48GB, reported free: ~6GB, but contiguous max chunk ~512MB.
elaine: Customer impact tracker: acct-110 and acct-221 report 20-40% failures on some prompts. CS alerted and started mitigation playbook.
maria: Tried soft-evicting KV cache on node-gpu-22 to free contiguous blocks, no reliable improvement. We also triggered scaledown of batch size for a canary deployment which reduced OOMs for a short window.
dylan: Hypothesis: fragmentation + small reserved allocations for prefetch are blocking large allocation requests. We need to either (a) force drain and restart to defragment, (b) move heavy traffic to fallback nodes, or (c) trigger runtime to consolidate reserves. Thoughts?
samir: Moving traffic is fastest. I'm starting a graceful drain of node-gpu-22 and routing model traffic to pool-gpu-09/10. Doing a canary at 10% first.
deploy-bot: Starting rollout: shift 10% traffic from cluster-gpu-22 to pool-gpu-09,pool-gpu-10.
dylan: While traffic shifts, can someone capture allocator debug trace on one reproducer container? Use `REDWOOD_ALLOC_LOG=debug` and `rdwctl dump-alloc --pid=12345 > /tmp/alloc.log`.
kai: Running alloc trace now, will attach once complete. Also collecting mini heap-profile and kv-cache stats.
maria: Observed a flurry of `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` at 2633337889 with traces pointing to a single large tokenization batch. Might be a pathological request size hitting worst-case fragmentation.
dylan: For immediate mitigation, reduce max tokens for affected models at routing layer and enable small-request preemption. I pushed a policy change to route over-limit requests to a fallback smaller model.
dylan: @samir confirm drain complete?
samir: Drain of node-gpu-22 80% done, tasks evicted. New traffic on pool-gpu-09 shows error rate down ~70%. Still seeing isolated OOMs on warmup containers.
elaine: CS update sent: temporary degraded throughput, failover in progress, ETA ~20m for full stabilization, customers notified.
kai: alloc.log uploaded to /var/log/incident/2633337890/alloc.log — shows many small free segments and repeated failed attempts to coalesce because reserved slab flags prevented merging.
maria: This looks like a reserve-tagging bug: when prefetch reserved blocks are tagged they block coalescing with freed chunks. Could explain headroom numbers but poor max contiguous size.
dylan: Action items: 1) engineering: reproduce locally and create reduced test to exercise reserve-tag coalesce path (owner: kai). 2) runtime fix: if cannot coalesce, fall back to spill to disk instead of OOM (owner: samir). 3) ops: add a temporary routing rule to keep large-batch requests off fragmented nodes until patched (owner: maria). 4) CS: update impacted customers and collect logs (owner: elaine).
elaine: I'll coordinate the customer updates and collect specific request IDs from acct-110/221/305 for postmortem.
kai: Started local repro using mixture of small/large allocs to emulate fragmentation. If I can reproduce, will open PR with failing test and patch suggestion.
dylan: Good. Also increasing logging window and enabling a short-term metric: max_contiguous_free_bytes per GPU to surface this earlier.
maria: Will add dashboard alert for max_contiguous_free_bytes < 1GB per GPU.
samir: Confirmed runtime restart on node-gpu-22 after drain cleared residual OOMs; container warmup succeeded and contiguous max chunk improved to ~3.2GB. Error rate down to baseline.
dylan: Marking incident as mitigated, but still P1 until root cause PR and deploy. Keeping incident open for postmortem and follow-up actions.
incident-bot: INC-2026-0421 status changed to mitigated. Oncall handoff: dylan -> kai for follow-up dev work.
maria: Thanks team. We'll schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow to cover repro, fix plan, and customer SLAs. :thumbsup:
